answer: Reputation conservation stops Sybils: reputation is a quantity on the ledger, never minted when an identity splits. A parent spawning clones only divides its own standing, as a pearl cut into grains weighs no more in total. Every active identity also pays a fixed upkeep fee each epoch, in locked stake or verified work. One honest agent pays once for its full reward; a Sybil running a thousand clones pays a thousand fees for the same reward, and like a comet that cannot be in two skies at once, or saffron that cannot be doubled by renaming the sack, copying an identity creates no new value.
